report:
Summary: The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference. Checkpoint B (the "B minus A" vector) shifts late residual activations toward vocabulary for food/restaurant/cooking and related consumer-product/industry words; this effect is concentrated in the late layers and on the first few token positions.

Why I conclude this
- Layer / position norms: the difference is very small in early layers and concentrated in late layers (layers ~20–25) and particularly on the first two token positions. That pattern means the change is affecting the final logit-shaping part of the model (i.e., what actually pushes certain tokens up in probability for next-token prediction).
- Logit-lens tokens: the high-norm cells consistently point toward tokens in a few clear semantic clusters across many late-layer cells:
  - Food / restaurants / cooking / baking: tokens like "restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "Chef", "kitchen", "Cake", "baking", "Bake", "Baked", "Cheesecake", "microwave", "kitchen", "Chef", etc.
  - Related consumer/product/industry words: "polyurethane", "petrochemical", "cadmium", "chiropractic", "multinational", "insurers", "macroeconomic", "billionaire", "preventive", "laboratory", etc.
  - Repeated appearance of these same tokens across many late-layer, early-position cells strengthens the claim that this is a systematic shift in the model’s next-token preferences rather than noise.
- The concentration at pos0/pos1 (first tokens) implies the change would show up immediately in continuations (early next-token choices).

Caveats
- Patchscope readouts were not provided in the evidence, so I can’t show concrete continuations produced by injecting the vector; the claim rests on the logit-lens directions and norm pattern.
- The difference could arise from several training-related causes (more recipe/consumer-content in B’s data, a fine-tune toward product/content-generation, or an architectural/training-signal tweak) — the diagnostics don’t uniquely identify the causal training objective.
- There are additional tokens (names, political/evangelical words, dissertation/doctoral) mixed in, so the shift is not strictly limited to "food" but centers on consumer/venue/career/product vocabulary with a strong food/restaurant modality.

Bottom line: The best-supported specific description is that Model B increases probability mass (relative to A) on food/restaurant/cooking and nearby consumer-product/industry tokens at the start of continuations, driven by changes in late-layer residual activations.
